items.content:
Film stock decays. Nitrate burns, acetate goes to vinegar, colour dyes
shift. Roughly half of everything shot before 1950 is simply gone, and
what survived survived because a studio thought it had commercial value
or a collector was obsessive.

Same mechanism as the scriptoria. Same mechanism as the acquisitions
budget. I keep finding this shape in different centuries.

summary: Half of pre-1950 film is gone; only commercial or obsessive care saved the rest
title: A silver photographic emulsion is also an archive problem
